args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1 to production, checkout-api failed health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. (Its staging build, v2.3.1-rc, was also marked unhealthy.) We rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before trying to deploy it again.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was live in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.2.9 was also healthy but older.
- **After the rollback:** all three regions are running v2.3.0, the service is passing health checks, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) says what failed, what we rolled back to, the recovered numbers, and that the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before.

The staging build of this release (v2.3.1-rc) was also marked unhealthy, but it still went to production. The post-incident review should check how the release process let that happen.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
